extracted.intended_audience: economists and researchers studying technological innovation and patent-based measures
extracted.subtask_description: Create indicators of technological innovation using high-dimensional textual analysis of patent documents to identify important and breakthrough patents, and to construct aggregate and sectoral time-series indices spanning the long run (1840–present).

rubrics_metrics.name: Important patents defined by textual similarity to past and future work
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify important patents based on textual similarity of a given patent to previous and subsequent work: these patents are distinct from previous work but related to subsequent innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors use high-dimensional textual analysis of patent documents to find patents that are both novel relative to prior art (distinct from previous work) and influential for later work (related to subsequent innovations). This measure is intended to capture patent importance beyond conventional indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakthrough innovations as right-tail of importance measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify breakthrough innovations as the most important patents—those in the right tail of our measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents with extreme (high) values of the importance indicator are labeled as breakthroughs and are used to characterize major technological advances and waves over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of aggregate and sectoral technology indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct time series indices of technological change at the aggregate and sectoral levels using the importance indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The indices track the evolution of technological waves across long time spans (1840 to the present) and can be decomposed by sector to show which technologies drive changes (examples given: electricity and transportation in the 1880s; chemicals and electricity in the 1920s–1930s; computers and communication post-1980s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage and scope for the measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The technology indices cover innovation by private and public firms as well as nonprofit organizations and the US government, spanning 1840 to the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The broad scope of patent sources and long time span are part of the methodological design, enabling analysis of long-run technological change across sectors and organizational types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation via correlation with existing patent quality measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance indicators correlate with existing measures of patent quality but also provide complementary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors compare their textual- similarity-based importance measures to conventional patent quality metrics to demonstrate both overlap and the novel information captured by their approach; this validation supports the measure's usefulness.
